title: Friction and Contact Forces
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Friction and Contact Forces Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify that forces can be exerted by one object on another by direct contact, such as pushes, pulls and friction, or from a distance (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on pushes, pulls, friction and air and water resistance, with examples from footy, cricket, surfing and bike riding. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Friction slows things down where surfaces touch.
key_sub: Contact forces act when objects touch; friction acts against the movement.
body_html:
How to think about it

Contact forces happen when objects touch: pushes, pulls and friction.

  • A force can start an object moving, stop it, speed it up, slow it down, change its direction or change its shape.
  • Friction acts between surfaces, against the direction of movement. Rough surfaces give more friction than smooth ones.
  • Air resistance and water resistance are kinds of friction. Streamlined shapes reduce them; parachutes increase air resistance.
Example

A box slides to the right. Which way does friction act?

friction acts against the movement

Answer: to the left

Example

Why do footy boots have studs?

studs dig into the grass

more grip

Answer: more friction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking smooth surfaces have no friction at all.
  • Thinking friction is always unhelpful (we need it to walk and to brake).
  • Thinking friction acts in the same direction as the movement.

faq.a: Friction is a force between two surfaces that rub together. It acts against the movement and slows things down.

faq.q: How can we increase or reduce friction?
faq.a: Rough surfaces, treads and grippy materials increase friction. Smooth surfaces, oil, wax on skis and wheels reduce it.

faq.q: Is air resistance a kind of friction?
faq.a: Yes. Air resistance is friction between a moving object and the air. Water resistance is friction with water.
